jamie-customer: hey support — invoice for acct acme-inc shows 720 reserved GPU hours for march but the console hourly aggregates show ~540. token burn was low that month, not sure where extra ~180 hours came from. pool: alpha-1. can someone look?

sarah-support: hi @jamie-customer :wave: sorry about the noise. can you paste the pool id (looks like you gave alpha-1), and any timestamps for spikes? we'll pull metering and the invoice line items.

jamie-customer: pool id is alpha-1-prod. i noticed a burst on 2024-03-12 ~02:00 UTC and a deploy around that time. our app had low request qps otherwise. attaching the billing invoice line (copied): `line_item: dedicated_capacity_hours: 720`

billing-bot: Invoice 2024-03-31 generated for account acme-inc. Dedicated capacity hours: 720.

tom-infra: pinging infra side — two things to check: warmup instances (autoscale ramp-up) get billed as full hour increments in the billing pipeline, while dashboard shows per-minute consumption. also check termination race where instances start+stop within same hour and aggregator rounds differently. can @kevin-metering run the hourly aggregates vs invoice join?

kevin-metering: running quick diffs now. preliminary: invoice sums do include a rounding rule: any instance active during an hour increments that hour. dashboard's hourly-aggregate job reports fractional usage by minute. i see a cluster of ~12 short-lived warmup replicas on 3/12 between 02:00-03:00 UTC that aggregated to ~180 billed hours after per-instance rounding. repro query I ran: ```sql
-- billed hours (billing pipeline)
SELECT sum(ceil(active_seconds/3600.0)) AS billed_hours
FROM instance_events
WHERE pool = 'alpha-1-prod' AND ts >= '2024-03-01' AND ts < '2024-04-01';

-- dashboard hours (per-minute aggregation)
SELECT sum(active_seconds)/3600.0 AS dashboard_hours
FROM instance_minute_agg
WHERE pool = 'alpha-1-prod' AND ts >= '2024-03-01' AND ts < '2024-04-01';
```

kevin-metering: tl;dr: billed_hours = 720, dashboard_hours ≈ 539.7. The delta (~180) maps to 12 instances that were up for <5 minutes each but crossed the hour boundary and got rounded up independently in billing. this looks like a double-accounting between warmup not being collapsed in billing.

jamie-customer: that makes sense — we had a canary rollout that spawned a bunch of short-lived machines. why does billing round per-instance rather than per-pool-hour? seems surprising.

tom-infra: historically billing used per-instance ceiling for committed capacity to simplify vendor invoicing. we can treat short-lived warmups as an optimization later. for now, options: 1) we can retroactively collapse warmup entries within same hour per pool and issue a credit, 2) patch billing pipeline to bucket by pool-hour, 3) provide guidance to teams about warmup policies to avoid spawn storms.

sarah-support: @jamie-customer we can do a one-time pro-rated credit for the ~180 hours while we implement a fix. will need accounting sign-off. can you confirm you'd like us to proceed with a credit and provide the billing contact?

jamie-customer: yes please, credit would be great. billing contact is lisa@acme-inc. thanks. :pray:

kevin-metering: next steps from metering side: open PR to change aggregator to bucket by pool-hour and add a migration to recompute affected months. I'll include a safeguard to ignore warmup-tagged instances for committed_hour calculation. ETA for PR + staging test: ~5 business days.

tom-infra: noted, i'll add an ops runbook note about canary spawn settings and recommend `max_warmup_replicas=2` for dedicated pools to avoid this in future.

billing-bot: Ticket created: BILL-4829 — "alpha-1-prod: pro-rated 180 GPU-hour credit request" assigned to sarah-support.

sarah-support: thanks everyone. @jamie-customer i'll follow up with accounting cc:lisa@acme-inc, expect update within 48h. :eyes: any further logs or deploy IDs helpful for the audit?

jamie-customer: deploy id `deploy-20240312-8f7a`. attaching our canary script snippet in case it's useful: ```bash
# canary spawn loop (internal)
for i in $(seq 1 12); do
airflow trigger_spawn --pool alpha-1-prod --warmup 30s &
done
```

kevin-metering: that snippet matches the short-lived events i see. i'll tag those events with `warmup:true` retroactively where we can.

jamie-customer: appreciate the quick triage — thanks all! :+1:
